Create a persistent session

Source: R/session_api.R
sas_session.Rd

A session holds the state kept between submissions: the WORK library and its metadata, macro variables and macro definitions, user formats (PROC FORMAT), system options set with OPTIONS, titles, filerefs and _LAST_. Pass it to sas_run() several times to run a program in several submissions. sas_run() without session runs in a fresh session that is discarded afterwards.

Usage

sas_session(work = list())

Arguments

work

Named list of data frames to load into WORK.

Value

A SasSession object (R6).

Details

Each submission starts outside syntax-check mode and with its own $status, $errors and $log in the returned result; SYSERR/SYSCC, like every other macro variable, carry over. The PROC SQL connection is opened on first use and closed by sas_session_close() (or when the session is garbage collected).

See also

sas_work(), sas_macro_vars(), sas_log()

Examples

s <- sas_session()
sas_run("data a; x = 1; run; %let n = 3;", session = s)
#> 
#> ── Log ──
#> 
#> No ERRORs or WARNINGs
#> 1          data a; x = 1; run; %let n = 3;
#> 
#> NOTE: The data set WORK.A has 1 observations and 1 variables.
#> ── WORK data sets ──
#> 
#> WORK.A: 1 obs, 1 vars
#> Levels: L1
res <- sas_run("data b; set a; y = x * &n; run;", session = s)
res$work$b
#> # A tibble: 1 × 2
#>       x     y
#>   <dbl> <dbl>
#> 1     1     3
sas_work(s)$a
#> # A tibble: 1 × 1
#>       x
#>   <dbl>
#> 1     1
sas_macro_vars(s)$n
#> [1] "3"
sas_session_close(s)
